messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired -> PROD-REDIS-CONN (severity: P1). Affected service: inference-proxy (hosted API). Symptoms: spike in 503s, client connection rejections from redis-primary-1, increased p99 token gen latency. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/P12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident P12345 assigned to oncall rotation (priority 1). Auto-escalation in 12m if not acknowledged.

alex.k: acked. jumping on it. any immediate customer-reported outages? :eyes:

sara.m: looking at dashboards — error rate on /v1/generate is up 8x, 503s correlate with spikes in redis client_conn_failures. charts: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/redis-clients

alex.k: can someone paste the redis logs from primary? suspect ERR max number of clients reached.

emily_s: pasted tail of redis log from redis-primary-1:
```
[36x] 2026-03-15 21:03:12.123 * Warning: 0 clients connected (maxclients: 1000).
[36x] 2026-03-15 21:03:12.456 # Server started, Redis version 6.2.8
[36x] 2026-03-15 21:04:01.789 # Error opening fd: can't accept new connections
[36x] 2026-03-15 21:04:12.002 - ERR max number of clients reached
```

mike_p: yep ERR max number of clients. client_count currently 1003 and climbing (we cap at 1000). Looks like a burst of inference-proxy connections not reusing pools.

alex.k: quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle new sessions at LB (rate-limit route /v1/generate) 2) bump redis maxclients to 5000 temporarily on primary 3) identify noisy app instances and restart to recycle connections 4) enable client-side connection pooling fallback (pgbouncer-like) — low-risk first two now.

sara.m: throttling rule pushed as a circuit-breaker on the gateway: `limit_req zone=genburst burst=50 nodelay` — deployed in edge canary. If we see reduced ingress, good.

ops-bot: deploy edge config to 4/4 nodes succeeded.

alex.k: bumping maxclients now on redis-primary-1 to 5000 via `CONFIG SET maxclients 5000` (temporary, will add to infra config later). command output:
```
127.0.0.1:6379> CONFIG SET maxclients 5000
OK
```

emily_s: after bump, client_count dropped to ~1200 due to backlog clearing, 503s started to fall. p95 latency improving but p99 still elevated.

mike_p: I'm going to drain one noisy inference-proxy pod found in infra metrics (ip 10.20.30.45) — it had 800+ outbound redis conns. restarting it now.

sara.m: restart complete, that pod's connections dropped, cluster connections went down ~600. charts look better. :thumbsup:

alex.k: good. next: find root cause — connection leak in proxy or insufficient pooling. capture strace/conn-trace on restarted pod and open an action ticket. tagging eng-runtime and devex for follow-up.

mike_p: creating ticket ENG-7721: "inference-proxy connection leak investigation" with logs and heap dump link. assigned to eng-runtime.

emily_s: customer impact note: Hosted API saw elevated error rates for ~7m window, estimated 0.8% of total requests failed (mostly short-lived). No enterprise SLA breaches reported yet, but flagging accounts with high QPS.

alex.k: handing over to night oncall @mike_p for monitoring and follow-up. I'll stay available for handoff questions.

mike_p: acked. will monitor for 30m, escalate if anything regresses. setting PD incident to monitored -> acknowledging so auto-escalation paused.

incident-bot: Incident P12345 status updated: acknowledged by alex.k, assigned to mike_p, severity P1 -> triaged. Actions taken: gateway throttling, CONFIG SET maxclients, pod restart. Post-incident follow-up: ENG-7721.

sara.m: quick postmortem TO-DOs: add stronger client pool limits in proxy, add redis connection alarm on per-instance threshold (not just aggregate), make maxclients config a managed infra param, add playbook steps for CONFIG SET + revert.

mike_p: I put a short blameless note in the incident doc: https://confluence.internal/incidents/P12345 and scheduled a 30m follow-up tomorrow 09:00 PT.

alex.k: great work team. closing slack thread for now — if anyone sees new errors ping oncall. :coffee:
